scan_linter_check.description:
Flags string literals that are 32-character hexadecimal values (sys_ids), in any script. A sys_id ties the script to one specific record: it breaks when that record is not on the target instance or has a different sys_id there, and it hides which record is meant.
Priority 3 (review), not blocking: sys_ids of records delivered in the same update set, or created identically on every instance, are legitimate; the reviewer decides. Replaces the sys_id part of the legacy check "NS: Hardcoded sys_ids, Emails, or Group Names".
scan_linter_check.name: SN-CFG-002: Hardcoded sys_id
scan_linter_check.resolution_details: Look the record up by a stable key (name, number, or a system property holding the sys_id) instead of embedding the sys_id. If the record is delivered with the same update set and the sys_id is stable across instances, mute the finding with a reason.
scan_linter_check.short_description: A string literal in a script is a sys_id.
